text:
Alex: seeing repeated p99 spikes in eu-west last night around 18:30-20:00 local. p95 fine but p99 jumps to ~420ms. can someone run admit-sensitivity for a +10% and +25% demand scenario?

Jon: noted. rough back-of-envelope: current fleet = 520 vGPUs across pool-a, effective token/s per GPU at our median seq = ~45k tok/s. p99 target = 400ms, p95 = 150ms. if arrival rate increases 10% then queue length jumps nonlinearly. will simulate. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Sasha: is this primarily due to burst traffic (startup customers) or steady elevated load? cost tradeoffs matter before we add capacity. :money_with_wings:

Alex: looks bursty + regional surge from partner replay tests. also some requests have larger context so variance high.

Priya: quick ask — can we try two knobs: stricter admission (lower max outstanding per-customer) vs short-term scale-up of 40 GPUs in eu-west? compare p99 and cost delta.

Jon: running a quick M/M/c-ish sensitivity to get ballpark. paste results:

```
scenario: baseline
fleet: 520 GPUs
service rate per gpu: 45k tok/s
median seq len: 750 tokens
est requests/sec: 820
p95 latency est: 150ms
p99 latency est: 380ms

scenario: +10% arrivals
est requests/sec: 902
p95 est: 160ms
p99 est: 520ms  <-- exceeds SLO

scenario: +25% arrivals
est requests/sec: 1025
p95 est: 190ms
p99 est: 820ms
```

Jon: simple numbers show p99 grows fast. admission needed to keep p99 <400ms for +10% without adding hardware.

Sasha: cost calc for adding 40 GPUs in eu-west (on-demand-equivalent):

```
40 gpus * $3.00/hr * 24 * 365 = $1,051,200/yr
```

Sasha: so year cost ~1.05M, compare to revenue risk / SLA penalties. also we can try autoscale burst (reserve for 6 hours/day) which is cheaper but operationally trickier.

Alex: agree. prefer admission first. can we craft an admission curve that is region-aware and traffic-shape-aware? e.g., allow higher admit during sustained low-variance periods, clamp during high variance bursts.

Priya: proposed config snippet for admit policy (test only):

```
admit_policy:
  region_bias:
    eu-west: 0.95
    us-east: 1.0
  window: 60s
  p99_threshold_ms: 400
  admit_curve: "(utilization < 0.7) ? 1.0 : (0.7-0.95) linear to 0.6 : 0.2"
  per_customer_max_inflight: 6
```

Priya: basically tighten per-customer inflight during high util and lower overall admit proportionally.

Jon: will run simulator with that curve and these demand spikes. quick run results (simulated):

- baseline admit_curve: p99=380ms (ok)
- +10% with region_bias only: p99=510ms (bad)
- +10% with admit_curve + per-customer cap: p99=360ms (good)
- +25% with admit curve: p99=680ms (still bad)

Jon: summary: admission tuning buys headroom for moderate bursts (+~10-12%) but not for sustained +25% type increases.

Sasha: for +25% sustained we either add GPUs or change model config (quantize or reduce max context) to improve service rate. cost to add 120 GPUs = 120*3*24*365 = $3,153,600/yr (ouch).

Alex: alternatives: temporary burst pool (reserve cheaper instances), or reroute non-critical traffic to cheap, lower-latency models. Also consider prefix cache warmup to reduce KV misses during partner replays.

Priya: action items:
- Jon: produce a 24-hr sensitivity run with realistic diurnal shape + partner replay pattern, output p95/p99 per hour for baseline, admit-tuned, and +40gpu scenarios (due EOD).
- Sasha: cost vs commit calc for 40/80/120 GPUs with reserved vs on-demand pricing (due tomorrow).
- Alex: draft a short runbook for region-aware admission toggle and safe rollback steps.

deploy-bot: scheduled canary toggle "admit-policy-eu-west-v2" ready for manual trigger. :robot_face:

infra-bot: noticed 3 network interface flaps on node pool-a-34 between 18:25-18:40, packet drops ~0.02% (not critical but increases variance). logged under INC-2026-221.

Sasha: add network variance to sensitivity — even small packet loss amplifies p99 for long tail contexts.

Alex: thanks team. prioritize admission roll and the sim. want clear SLO gates: if p99 > 500ms for more than 15m escalate to on-call and consider burst add.

Priya: noted. i'll put the gate into escalation policy.

Jon: running sim now, will post results in this thread. :thinking:
